lede: Korean lyric coloratura soprano · recitalist · opera singer · voice faculty.
body_html:
Dr. Jiyeon Hwang is a Korean lyric coloratura soprano known for her distinctive vocal range and bright, sweet timbre. She has performed extensively in operatic roles, recitals, and concerts across the United States, Italy, the Czech Republic, and South Korea.

Dr. Hwang received her Bachelor of Music in Voice Performance from Chung-Ang University in Korea with a full tuition scholarship and admission with highest distinction. She earned her Master of Music in Voice Performance from the Manhattan School of Music in 2015, where she studied under soprano Catherine Malfitano. She completed her Doctor of Musical Arts in Voice Performance from the University of Minnesota as a Harvey V. Berneking Scholarship recipient. Her doctoral thesis examined early Korean opera composers Jaemyung Hyun and Isang Yun, and the soprano arias of Chunhyang-Jeon and Sim Tjong.

Currently, Dr. Hwang is an Assistant Professor of Voice and Choir at Texas A&M International University, where she leads the voice and choir programs and teaches Applied Voice, Applied Studio Class, Junior and Senior Performance, Choir Ensemble, Voice Method, and Art Song Literature. In 2019, she received the Graduate Research Partnership, performing the roles of Zerlina in Don Giovanni and Lisette in La Rondine at the Mediterranean Opera Studio in Sicily, Italy.

Awards & honors

Dr. Hwang was selected as the representative singer of the North Central Chapter of the National Association of Teachers of Singing (NATS) to compete in the Artist Auditions in January 2022 in New York, where she won the William Vennard Award from NATSAA (National Round). She received the Gold Award from the Forte International Music Competition and Third Prize at the San Francisco International Innovative Music Competition (2021), and was named a Finalist at both The Century Opera Competition and the Tri-Cities Opera Resident Program. Her earlier honors include First Prize in the Kenwood Symphony Orchestra Concerto Competition and Second Prize in the NATS competition (2018).

She performed at Weill Recital Hall at Carnegie Hall in 2022 as the Winner's Concert of the Forte International Music Competition.

Innovation — “Webpera”

During the pandemic, she pioneered a new genre of virtual opera, Webpera (Web + Opera), with the worldwide premiere of L'elisir d'amore in collaboration with Camerata New Jersey. She was also cast as Berta in The Barber of Seville with the Cleveland Opera Theatre in 2020.
